overview: This table tells the game which animations a shikigami uses in battle and which poses appear in character views and Situation Overview.
description: Shikigami animation-set rows: parallel FName arrays pairing named animation slots (for example Idle, Run or AttackA_01_01) with AnimMontage primary-asset names. Battle sets are attached to ShikigamiDataTable rows; separate rows supply character-capture and Situation Overview poses.

ID.simple: The name that identifies this group of shikigami animations. The game uses it to connect the group to a shikigami, a character view, or a Situation Overview pose.
ID.technical: Export field ID is native Id (FName) and the DataTable row key (ImportKeyField=Id); no runtime consumer reads the Id member of this struct directly. ShikigamiDataTable.Id_ShikigamiAnimation holds these IDs: the 20 exported Shikigami rows reference 71 battle sets (base, _DAMAGE and per-_ATTACK* rows), with None padding skipped. The other 13 rows are reached from CharacterCaptureDataTable.Id_ShikigamiCharacterAnimation (CN_080_CHARACTER_CAPTURE) or SituationOverviewPoseDataTable.Id_ShikigamiCharacterAnimation_Ally/_Enemy (six ally and six enemy poses). Lookups use FindRow<T> over ShikigamiAnimationDataTables (DTM +0x6E0): the shared collector in battle preload and level-sequence preload, an inline search in battle spawn, and FindRow in capture. All finders return the first matching row while walking the table array; the manager registers one table and the export contains 84 unique row keys.

Key.simple: The action an animation belongs to, such as idle, running, jumping, or attacking. Situation Overview uses these names for ally or enemy poses, and other character views use only idle and entry animations.
Key.technical: Export Key is native TArray<FName> Key. All 84 exported rows have 33 Key entries and 33 Filename entries, right-padded with NAME_None (2,451 None pairs); no row repeats a non-None key. Battle spawn walks Key.Num(), skips a pair when either Key[i] or FileName[i] is None, and calls UGameAnimInstance::SetAnimationAsset(Key[i], Montage, false). That stores the montage pointer and its BlendIn/BlendOut times in the anim instance's FName-keyed AssetMap without duplicating the object; a later duplicate key would overwrite the earlier entry. Capture setup builds a Key->FileName TMap: Situation Overview keeps every non-None pair from the pose's ally/enemy row, while other capture types keep at most the idle and enter key names from CharacterCapture (ShikigamiCharacterIdleAnimationKey and ShikigamiCharacterEnterAnimationKey). Playback helpers that consume those keys use FindChecked. CN_010 starts Idle, Run, DashBegin, Dash, DashEnd, JumpBegin, JumpUp, JumpTop, Summon, SummonAir.

Filename.simple: The name a modder changes to swap the animation used for an action, such as idle or attacking. In Situation Overview, the first animation in the list sets the shikigami's pose.
Filename.technical: Export Filename is native TArray<FName> FileName (the catalog spelling differs from the header). Values are exact FName keys for GamePrimaryAssetType_AnimMontage loaders, not object paths. Battle preload's collector appends the entire FileName array, including None padding, to the animation-name list; GamePrimaryAssetLoader_CreateLoaders then skips None names, deduplicates repeats and creates StudioShikigamiAnimLoaders_400, which is later retained in StudioRetainedLoaders_90. BattleBase independently builds StudioAnimMontageLoaders_810 from the same collector; at spawn it uses FindChecked on each non-None filename, resolves the loaded montage through the Abrams asset manager and installs it under Key[i]. A null montage is a no-op in SetAnimationAsset. Capture puts the mapped names into per-slot AnimMontageLoaders and plays them directly; Situation Overview pose playback indexes FileName[0] without checking array length or None. Every exported row has equal 33-element arrays, but the indexed consumers trust Key.Num(): a shorter FileName array would be out of bounds, while extra filenames beyond Key.Num() are ignored there (though preload still collects them).

notes: Manager/loader chain: ShikigamiAnimationDataTables is DTM slot +0x6E0; the sole ShikigamiAnimationDataTable primary asset is resolved into that array at GameDataTableManager.cpp:240, and its name is added to the DataTable loader list at line 412. Finders walk the table array in first-match order; this export/code has one table and no repeated row keys, so no cross-shard precedence applies.

The struct has only Id, Key and FileName: no numeric fields, units, timings, blend overrides or state-machine data. UGameAnimInstance copies the referenced montage's own BlendIn/BlendOut times and later PlayAnimationAsset can override them; the row itself only selects montage FNames. Playback is triggered by C++ controllers through the same FName keys. Retail Blueprint assets are not present in the source or these exports, and no BP-only behavior is asserted here.

Export shape: one asset with 84 rows, 33 Key/Filename slots in every row and NAME_None right-padding. 71 rows are referenced from Shikigami battle sets; the other 13 are one character-capture row plus six ally and six enemy Situation Overview pose rows. There are no localized or numbered shards of this table in the export, and the struct constructor supplies no default rows or slot values.

Level sequences consume this table indirectly: BattleAssets_Shikigami_12BD9B0 collects its filenames into StudioAnimMontageLoaders_7C0, but the reconstructed level-sequence shikigami spawn path installs only CharacterAnimation rows on the anim instance; it does not install these ShikigamiAnimation rows.

NAME_None is the sentinel for unused row IDs, keys and filenames. Callers skip None IDs and key/file pairs in the indexed paths; loader creation also drops None names, but the preload collector copies them into its intermediate name array first.

usages.detail: Resolves the loaded ShikigamiAnimationDataTable into the manager's ShikigamiAnimationDataTables array (+0x6E0); the loader name is registered at line 412.
Shared collector: Character.Id_CharacterShikigami to CharacterShikigami.Id_Shikigami to Shikigami.Id_ShikigamiAnimation to this row; appends the whole FileName array (retail 0x12bd9b0).

Battle preload calls that collector for every slot and creates AnimMontage loaders in StudioShikigamiAnimLoaders_400; loader creation skips None and duplicate names, and GamePhase.cpp:248 retains the map across phase change.

Battle spawn looks up each non-None Key/Filename pair, resolves the montage from the separately built StudioAnimMontageLoaders_810 via the asset manager, and files it in the shikigami anim instance under Key (bDuplicate=false).
Capture setup resolves the capture row's Id_ShikigamiCharacterAnimation, or the pose's ally/enemy ID for Situation Overview, and builds a filtered Key->FileName map.

Situation Overview idle playback resolves the pose's animation row and plays the montage named by FileName[0] on the spawned shikigami; other capture types use PlayShikigamiIdleMontage/PlayShikigamiEnterMontage with FindChecked on the mapped key.
Level-sequence preload uses the shared collector to add these filenames to StudioAnimMontageLoaders_7C0; the reconstructed cutscene spawn path does not install them on the shikigami anim instance.
Indirect cache consumer: controllers call PlayAnimationAsset with these Key FNames to look up the montage previously installed by SetAnimationAsset.
